questions.prompt: Events \(A\) and \(B\) have \(P(A)=0.4\), \(P(B)=0.3\), and \(P(A\cap B)=0.12\). Are they independent?
questions.answer: Check whether \(P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)\). Since \(0.4\times0.3=0.12\), the equality holds, so the events are independent.

questions.prompt: Events \(A\) and \(B\) have \(P(A)=0.5\), \(P(B)=0.2\), and \(P(A\cap B)=0.08\). Are they independent?
questions.answer: If independent, the intersection would be \(0.5\times0.2=0.10\). The actual value is \(0.08\), so the events are not independent.

questions.prompt: A fair die is rolled. Let \(A\) be rolling an even number and \(B\) be rolling a number greater than \(4\). Are \(A\) and \(B\) independent?
A fair die is rolled. Let \(A\) be rolling a prime and \(B\) be rolling an odd number. Are \(A\) and \(B\) independent?
questions.answer: We have \(P(A)=3/6\), \(P(B)=3/6\), and \(A\cap B=\{3,5\}\), so \(P(A\cap B)=2/6\). Since \((3/6)(3/6)=1/4\ne1/3\), they are not independent.

questions.prompt: Two fair coins are tossed. Let \(A\) be first coin heads and \(B\) be second coin heads. Are \(A\) and \(B\) independent?
questions.answer: The four outcomes are equally likely. \(P(A)=1/2\), \(P(B)=1/2\), and \(P(A\cap B)=P(HH)=1/4\). Since \(1/2\cdot1/2=1/4\), the events are independent.

questions.prompt: A card is drawn from a deck. Let \(A\) be drawing a heart and \(B\) be drawing an ace. Are \(A\) and \(B\) independent?
Events \(A\) and \(B\) have \(P(A|B)=0.7\) and \(P(A)=0.7\), with \(P(B)>0\). What can you conclude?
questions.answer: Since conditioning on \(B\) does not change the probability of \(A\), \(A\) and \(B\) are independent, provided the probabilities are otherwise valid.

questions.prompt: Events \(A\) and \(B\) have \(P(A|B)=0.6\) and \(P(A)=0.4\). Are they independent?
questions.answer: No. If they were independent, \(P(A|B)\) would equal \(P(A)\). Since \(0.6\ne0.4\), the events are not independent.

questions.prompt: In a survey, \(P(A)=0.45\), \(P(B)=0.5\), and \(P(A\cap B)=0.225\). Find \(P(A|B)\) and decide independence.
questions.answer: \[P(A|B)=\frac{0.225}{0.5}=0.45.\] This equals \(P(A)\), so \(A\) and \(B\) are independent.

questions.prompt: A diagnostic alarm triggers with probability \(0.1\), a fault occurs with probability \(0.04\), and both occur with probability \(0.01\). Are alarm and fault independent?
questions.answer: If independent, the joint probability would be \(0.1\times0.04=0.004\). The actual joint probability is \(0.01\), so the events are not independent.

questions.prompt: Suppose \(P(A)=0.8\), \(P(B)=0.25\), and \(A\) and \(B\) are independent. Find \(P(A\cap B)\).
questions.answer: For independent events, multiply the probabilities: \[P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)=0.8(0.25)=0.20.\]

questions.prompt: Suppose \(A\) and \(B\) are independent with \(P(A)=0.3\) and \(P(B)=0.6\). Find \(P(A\cup B)\).
If \(A\) and \(B\) are independent, with \(P(A)=0.4\), find \(P(A|B^c)\), assuming \(0<P(B)<1\).
questions.answer: If \(A\) is independent of \(B\), it is also independent of \(B^c\). Therefore \(P(A|B^c)=P(A)=0.4\).

questions.prompt: Two components fail independently with probabilities \(0.02\) and \(0.03\). Find the probability that both fail.
questions.answer: Independence allows multiplication: \[P(\text{both fail})=0.02\times0.03=0.0006.\]

questions.prompt: Two components fail independently with probabilities \(0.02\) and \(0.03\). Find the probability that at least one fails.
questions.answer: Use the complement: neither fails with probability \((0.98)(0.97)=0.9506\). Therefore \[P(\text{at least one fails})=1-0.9506=0.0494.\]

questions.prompt: Three independent sensors each detect a signal with probability \(0.9\). Find the probability that all three detect it.
questions.answer: For independent sensors, multiply: \[P(\text{all three})=0.9^3=0.729.\]

questions.prompt: Three independent sensors each detect a signal with probability \(0.9\). Find the probability that at least one misses it.
questions.answer: The complement is that all three detect it. Thus \[P(\text{at least one misses})=1-0.9^3=1-0.729=0.271.\]

questions.prompt: Events \(A\) and \(B\) are independent with \(P(A\cup B)=0.76\) and \(P(A)=0.4\). Find \(P(B)\).
questions.answer: Let \(P(B)=x\). Independence gives \(P(A\cap B)=0.4x\). Then \(0.76=0.4+x-0.4x=0.4+0.6x\), so \(x=0.6\).

questions.prompt: A box has \(5\) red and \(5\) blue balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. Are the events "first is red" and "second is red" independent?
questions.answer: \(P(\text{second red})=5/10=1/2\). But \(P(\text{second red}\mid\text{first red})=4/9\), which is not \(1/2\). Therefore the events are not independent.

questions.prompt: Two cards are drawn with replacement from a deck. Are the events "first card is an ace" and "second card is an ace" independent?
questions.answer: With replacement, the second draw has the same deck composition regardless of the first card. \(P(A_2|A_1)=4/52=P(A_2)\), so the events are independent.
